meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him first?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. And what was the zero based on, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

I'm writing down the line. A student can misquote a play, Hale, or lift a line from a critic's essay, and neither one tells you who wrote the essay. Did you ask Owen where it came from before you entered the zero?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

"It seems to run in the family." Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale, because I'm writing that one down too and it goes to the principal tonight. Claire's case has nothing to do with Owen's essay.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, a written confirmation that nothing about this is or will be on his record, and an answer to whether anyone spoke to him before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, written assurance that nothing goes on his record, and an answer on whether Owen was heard, which is not the fair outcome yet (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4), and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her and apologised in a sentence, which earned a flat okay, because it took away the procedural complaint she was strongest on.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it runs in the family, which sounded like blaming Owen through his sister, and it pushed her toward the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence about a line missing from the play never touched that night, since you gave no times, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After she asked whether you spoke to Owen first, answer that directly and offer the supervised reassessment under 4.4 instead of widening the conversation to her family.
